themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked 450% THIS WEEK to 22 complaints vs. a 4.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.69), signaling a sudden collapse in sanitation services or a coordinated community response to visible street conditions in East New York/Cypress Hills.
evidence: 22 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly baseline (450% spike, z-score: 3.69)
Concurrent 234% spike in 'Dirty Condition' complaints 2 weeks ago (61 complaints vs. 18.2 avg), suggesting sustained sanitation failure
Graffiti complaints up 743% last week (39 vs. 4.6 avg), indicating broader neighborhood deterioration
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to determine if street sweeping routes were cut, delayed, or reassigned this week
Interview residents and local business owners about visible accumulation of garbage/debris and impact on storefronts and foot traffic

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge on Streets
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped 127% THIS WEEK to 17 complaints vs. a 7.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.18), a sharp reversal of the typical residential noise decline and suggesting new street-level activity, construction, or vendor congestion.
evidence: 17 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.5 weekly average (127% spike, z-score: 7.18)
Concurrent mobile food vendor complaints exploded 2300% last week (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline), suggesting vendor-driven street noise
Residential noise DOWN 36% this week, indicating noise source is external/commercial rather than domestic
reporting_angles: Investigate whether unlicensed or high-volume mobile food vendors (carts, trucks) have proliferated on key commercial corridors this week
Map 311 complaints to identify which blocks are most affected and observe street activity during peak hours

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged 743% LAST WEEK to 39 complaints vs. a 4.6 weekly average (z-score: 8.28), the second-highest statistical anomaly in the district, signaling either a coordinated tagging campaign or a sudden visibility crisis in East New York/Cypress Hills.
evidence: 39 graffiti complaints last week vs. 4.6 weekly baseline (743% spike, z-score: 8.28, severity: high)
Concurrent spike in missing street signs (196% up, 10 vs. 3.4 avg), suggesting infrastructure damage or neglect
Part of broader sanitation collapse: dirty conditions up 234%, street sweeping complaints up 450%
reporting_angles: Scout major corridors (Atlantic Avenue, Jamaica Avenue, Broadway) to document extent and style of graffiti; determine if linked to specific gang or crew
Contact NYPD and Parks Department about response timeline and whether graffiti removal has been deprioritized

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped 129% LAST WEEK to 200 complaints vs. an 87.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.61), accelerating a chronic problem and blocking streets/driveways at a rate nearly 3x normal, with 2,200 blocked driveway complaints over 90 days showing systemic parking chaos.
evidence: 200 abandoned vehicle complaints last week vs. 87.4 weekly average (129% spike, z-score: 5.61)
4,551 illegal parking complaints over 90 days and 2,200 blocked driveway complaints, indicating parking pressure across district
Abandoned vehicles are second-highest spike after mobile food vendors, suggesting a specific trigger event or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Interview residents about where abandoned vehicles are concentrated and how long they typically sit before removal
Contact Sanitation/NYPD to determine if there was a processing backlog, reduced towing capacity, or deferred vehicle auctions last week

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked 2300% LAST WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline, z-score: 8.69), the highest statistical anomaly in the district, suggesting a sudden influx of carts or trucks that may be unlicensed, linked to street noise complaints, and concentrated in high-foot-traffic areas.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69, highest spike in district)
Concurrent 127% spike in street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK (17 vs. 7.5 avg), likely vendor-driven
524 building permits filed in 90 days but vendor infrastructure not addressed in ULURP pipeline
reporting_angles: Canvass commercial corridors to identify newly arrived food carts/trucks; check licensing and health permits with Department of Consumer Affairs
Interview local business owners about vendor competition and whether unlicensed operators are undercutting licensed vendors
